How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

   City Council Special Meeting Agenda
  Wednesday, April 24, 2024

  •  CALL TO ORDER
  •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

  1. STUDY SESSION

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 BUDGET STUDY SESSION FOR PROPOSED CITY
  OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM

  The preliminary Operating Budget and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) for
  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 are submitted to the City Council for initial review,
  facilitating a detailed examination of the proposed figures and seeking further
  guidance. Total proposed city-wide operating revenues total $85,300,000, with
  corresponding expenditures totaling $82,247,000. The general fund comprises
  revenues of $54,511,000 and expenditures of $53,738,000, resulting in a
  positive net change in fund balance of $773,000. The city-wide expenditure
  figures include $3,053,000 for new capital improvement projects.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025 proposed operating budget and capital improvement program; and
  provide direction to staff, as appropriate.

  2. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, May 7, 2024, at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at
www.sangabrielcity.com/agendacenter, or in person at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
San Gabriel, CA 91776. Materials related to an item on this Agenda, submitted to the City
Council after distribution of the Agenda packet, will be posted on the City website.

MINUTES OF APRIL 24, 2024
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 5:34 P.M. on
  Wednesday, April 24, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Denise Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director
  Rebecca Perez, Public Works Director/City Engineer
  Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,

I  Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Assistant City Clerk Marilyn
  Bonus, and Management Assistant Adam Yang.

  1. STUDY SESSION

  A. FISCAL VEAR 2024-2025 BUDGET STUDY SESSION FOR PROPOSED CITY
  OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation and City Manager Lazzaretto
  provided additional information on key items.

  Discussion included sales tax allocation based on point-of-sale versus point-of-use
  transactions; methodology for building permit and parking fine projections;
  improving communication of parking regulations; Community Development plan
  review and entitlement fee projections and use of consultants; Mission Playhouse
  deficit presentation in the Budget and Foundation status; details of park
  enhancements; Police Department grant-writing, recruitment, staffing alternatives,
  and overtime; details of the CASP program and administrative fines; equity-
  adjustment details; five-year projection methodology; sales tax details; plumbing

I  and electrical permit revenue projected increases; reserves and capital replacement
  fund details; funding for a future public safety facility; kudos for the Budget
  presentation; forecasted income increase from Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 to FY 2025-
  26 includes exchange of Proposition A funds and accounts for $500,000 in one-
  time spending in FY 2024-25; City-owned rental properties and cell tower lease
  income/expense; property tax revenue projection details; proposed new assistant
  director positions; and Neighborhood Improvement Services staffing details.

  There was no public comment.

   2.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:28 P.M.
